All declarations in this unit are complete definitions, record infrastructure or generated typeclass witnesses. admissible contains only analytic hypotheses and the exact measurable component-oracle contract, with no accuracy, runtime or execution-success premise. allowedAlgorithm identifies the computed factory. The convergence and actual-cost proofs remain in separately planned units.

The three smoothness inequalities exactly specialize the external weighted definitions to uniform weights 1/m; the importance factor m*w_i cancels. Differentiability makes the gradients genuine derivatives. A finite mean-square bound implies each component gradient is Lipschitz with bound sqrt(m)*Lplus; if a strictly positive source local constant is needed, enlarge this bound by 1. Hence the source component-smoothness premise is recoverable, including Lplus=0. The lower/gap pair avoids infimum attainment assumptions and uses supplied Delta as an upper bound. Current source inspection confirms the serial interface contains only analytic assumptions and a jointly measurable exact component oracle on one common full-measure event. It has no worker timing, large-sample, liveness or scheduling-independence premise.

Objective is the arithmetic mean over Fin m. The mean-square and centered inequalities use 1/m, squared component norms and the exact subtraction of squared objective-gradient differences. Their bounds are Lplus^2 and Lpm^2 times ||x-y||^2. Objective smoothness uses Lminus times ||x-y||. The visible accuracy criterion uses squared norm <=epsilon, matching the source rate 2*Delta/(eta*K).
